title: Compatibility with the coefficient tower
statement:
The transition morphisms $P_{n+1}\to P_n$ make each of the four corner
families an object
$$
 A_\bullet,B_\bullet,C_\bullet,D_\bullet
 \in D(\operatorname{Tow}_{A}(Y'))
$$
after restriction of scalars, and make $h,h',v,v'$ morphisms in this derived
tower category. Evaluation at $n$ recovers the four displayed corners and
arrows. The rectangle equation commutes with every transition and with every
compatible endomorphism of $K$.
The specified strict tower constructions are those of [def-weil-pbc-completed-four-towers].

note:
*Source note:* no Stacks Project entry states this tower-level datum. Stacks
describes the completed pullback and its reductions for a single object
(Lemma 61.20.2, [Tag 099N](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/099N)), the
proper base-change isomorphism (Theorem 61.30.1, [Tag
09C9](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09C9)) and, for a constructible
$K$, the structure of its reduction tower: Lemma 61.29.2 ([Tag
09C2](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09C2)) gives $K=\Rlim K_n$ with
$K_n=K\otimes^L_\Lambda\underline{\Lambda/I^n}$ of tor amplitude in a fixed
interval $[a,b]$, with constructible cohomology sheaves and of the form
$K_n=\epsilon^{-1}L_n$ for $L_n\in D_{ctf}(X_{\Et},\Lambda/I^n)$. The
derived-tower bookkeeping itself is the blueprint's (the derived inverse
limit and the bounded constructible tower), and no entry makes the four
corner families objects of the derived tower category; the blueprint adds
the transition data, the compatibility of the rectangle with every
transition and with compatible endomorphisms of $K$, and the identification
of the $n$-th evaluations with the finite-level corners.

proof.text: Apply the evaluation conjunct of the existing strict-tower exchange mate normalization at level n. This supplies the four evaluation isomorphisms and the four specified edge equations. Its proof retains the finite-level rectangle and quotient coefficient normalizations.
Expand the specified definition v prime = h inverse followed by v and h prime; cancel h with its inverse and use associativity for the strict rectangle.
Specialize exchangeStrict_naturality from the same existing normalization module to an endomorphism of K.

split_report.summary: Replaced the unsupported normalization-implies-strictness inference by two functorial strict reduction complexes and explicit transport through the horizontal projection-formula isomorphisms. Proved quotient and object naturality by transposing the counit formula, then used the finite-level rectangle to identify the transported fourth edge. Proved the rectangle and endomorphism identities in the derived tower category before evaluation. No new nodes or coefficient-category identifications.

old_proof.text: Work after restriction to the coefficient sheaf $A_{Y'}$, retaining the $P_n$-linear identifications at evaluation. Write $M=Lg^*Rf_*K$, $E=Lg'^*K$, $N=Rf'_*E$ and $e=\Ex^A_{\square,K}:M\to N$. Apply the functorial strict reduction construction of [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum] on $Y'$ to $M$ and $N$: set $\widetilde A_\bullet=R(M)$ and $\widetilde C_\bullet=R(N)$, represented by $QM\otimes_{A_{Y'}}(P_n)_{Y'}$ and $QN\otimes_{A_{Y'}}(P_n)_{Y'}$ with chain transitions $1\otimes q_n$. Their evaluations are $M\otimes_A^LP_n$ and $N\otimes_A^LP_n$. The canonical tensor/pullback identification used in [def-weil-pbc-four-arrows] identifies the former with $A_n$, and the latter is $C_n$ by [def-weil-pbc-four-corners]. This identification uses the same tensor associativity map for every coefficient: on representatives it reassociates the tensor factors, so replacing $P_{n+1}$ by $P_n$ on either side gives the same map. The transitions therefore become $a_{n+1,n}=Lg_n^*(1\otimes q_n)$ and $c_{n+1,n}=1\otimes q_n$, with the level-changing coefficients understood by restriction of scalars. Functorial reduction gives $\widetilde v=R(e):\widetilde A_\bullet\to\widetilde C_\bullet$, evaluating to $v_n$. The quotient identities give the strict transition cocycle, and functoriality gives $c_{n+1,n}v_{n+1}=v_na_{n+1,n}$. No claim that arbitrary diagrams in a derived category strictify is used.

old_proof.text: Check the projection-formula comparisons with both the quotient and the object variable. For a coefficient map $q:P\to P'$, transpose the two composites from $(Rf_*F)\otimes^LP$ to $Rf_*(F\otimes^LLf^*P')$ under $Lf^*\dashv Rf_*$. By [def-weil-pbc-projection-formula-map], both transposes are $(\varepsilon_F\otimes1)\circ(1\otimes Lf^*q)=(1\otimes Lf^*q)\circ(\varepsilon_F\otimes1)$, where the equality is tensor bifunctoriality (the two factors act on different tensor slots). The adjunction bijection thus gives $Rf_*(1\otimes Lf^*q)\pi_{f,F,P}=\pi_{f,F,P'}(1\otimes q)$. For $u:F\to F'$, the counit naturality identity $u\varepsilon_F=\varepsilon_{F'}Lf^*Rf_*u$ gives in exactly the same way $Rf_*(u\otimes1)\pi_{f,F,P}=\pi_{f,F',P}(Rf_*u\otimes1)$. Apply the first identity to $q_n$ for $(f,K)$ and $(f',E)$, and apply $Lg^*$ to the first square. With the tensor/pullback identifications of [def-weil-pbc-four-arrows], this yields $b_{n+1,n}h_{n+1}=h_na_{n+1,n}$ and $d_{n+1,n}h'_{n+1}=h'_nc_{n+1,n}$, where $b_{n+1,n}=Lg^*Rf_*(K_{n+1}\to K_n)$ and $d_{n+1,n}=Rf'_*(E_{n+1}\to E_n)$. Here $E_{n+1}\to E_n$ is $Lg'^*$ of the quotient map of $K$, identified with $1\otimes q_n$ through the functorial reduction identification of [def-weil-pbc-four-corners]. The second identity proves that these comparisons also intertwine the endomorphisms induced by any $\phi:K\to K$ and $Lg'^*\phi$.

old_proof.text: The arrows $h_n,h'_n$ are isomorphisms by [def-weil-pbc-four-arrows]; the applicable substantive input is the perfect projection formula [lemma-weil-pbc-perfect-projection-formula], since every $P_n$ is perfect in [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]. It applies to $E$ as well as $K$: it imposes no completeness assumption on the object variable. Realize $B_\bullet$ by the same strict complex as $\widetilde A_\bullet$, but identify its $n$-th evaluation with the named corner $B_n$ through $h_n:A_n\simeq B_n$. Realize $D_\bullet$ by the same strict complex as $\widetilde C_\bullet$, identifying evaluation with $D_n$ through $h'_n:C_n\simeq D_n$. Under these identifications their transitions are $h_na_{n+1,n}h_{n+1}^{-1}=b_{n+1,n}$ and $h'_nc_{n+1,n}(h'_{n+1})^{-1}=d_{n+1,n}$ by step 2. Thus these complexes realize precisely the required corner families and quotient transitions after restriction of scalars. Let $h:\widetilde A_\bullet\to B_\bullet$ and $h':\widetilde C_\bullet\to D_\bullet$ be the identity morphisms of the chosen representing complexes; their evaluations, read through the specified corner identifications, are $h_n,h'_n$. Transport of a realization through displayed evaluation isomorphisms is just relabeling the evaluated objects, not an assertion of an equivalence between $D(\operatorname{Tow})$ and $\operatorname{Tow}(D)$.

old_proof.text: Define the remaining derived-tower arrow by $v'=h'\widetilde v h^{-1}:B_\bullet\to D_\bullet$. Its $n$-th evaluation, under the corner identifications, is $h'_nv_nh_n^{-1}$. The finite-level rectangle [lem-weil-pbc-finite-level-rectangle] says $v'_nh_n=h'_nv_n$, so this evaluation is exactly the prescribed finite-level exchange $v'_n$ of [def-weil-pbc-four-arrows], including its transported etale-origin witness. Associativity gives $v'h=h'\widetilde v$ in $D(\operatorname{Tow}_{A}(Y'))$ itself. Compatibility with each quotient is also explicit: $d_{n+1,n}v'_{n+1}=h'_nc_{n+1,n}v_{n+1}h_{n+1}^{-1}=h'_nv_na_{n+1,n}h_{n+1}^{-1}=v'_nb_{n+1,n}$. Combined with steps 1 and 2 this proves that all four evaluated arrows respect the original quotient transitions and that evaluation recovers the given rectangle. The equality in the derived tower category was constructed before evaluation; it is not inferred from equality of all evaluations.

old_proof.text: For a compatible endomorphism $\phi:K\to K$, put $m=Lg^*Rf_*\phi$ and $z=Rf'_*Lg'^*\phi$. The ambient exchange of [def-weil-pbc-ambient-ringed-exchange] is a transformation of functors, so its naturality gives $ze=em$. Functorial reduction of [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum] therefore gives $R(z)\widetilde v=\widetilde vR(m)$ as an equality of derived-tower morphisms. Give $B_\bullet,D_\bullet$ the transported actions $hR(m)h^{-1}$ and $h'R(z)(h')^{-1}$. Their evaluations are respectively $Lg_n^*Rf_*\phi_n$ and $Rf'_*Lg_n'^*\phi_n$ by the object-naturality computation of step 2 and the functorial identifications in [def-weil-pbc-four-corners]. The actions on $\widetilde A_\bullet,\widetilde C_\bullet$ evaluate to the specified ambient actions. Conjugation now gives equivariance of $h,h'$ and $v'$, and the already proved equality $v'h=h'\widetilde v$ is equivariant. Since all actions and arrows are morphisms of the exhibited strict-tower realizations, these identities commute with every transition. This verifies the endomorphism clause without any additional assumption on $\phi$ beyond the given compatibility.
